* Synthetic OpenAir fixture for openair_db classification + geometry tests.
*
* Hand-written: no vendor data is reproduced. Every polygon is a 1-degree square
* placed on a grid so each case can be probed at a distinct, obvious point, and
* every name is invented EXCEPT the airspace-type words themselves, which are
* what the classifier keys on.
*
* Grid (lon runs 0..9 east, lat 40..41 for every square):
*   lon 0-1  ALPHA CTR            AC CTR   -> CTR      indexed
*   lon 1-2  BRAVO TMA            AC D     -> TMA      indexed via NAME keyword
*   lon 2-3  CHARLIE CTA          AC C     -> CTA      indexed via NAME keyword
*   lon 3-4  DELTA FIR            AC A     -> FIR      indexed via NAME keyword
*   lon 4-5  FREE RT ASPC ZZ      AC C     -> OTHER    NOT indexed  <-- the gap
*   lon 5-6  ECHO                 AC D     -> OTHER    NOT indexed  <-- the gap
*   lon 6-7  R-FOXTROT (RANGE)    AC R     -> OTHER    NOT indexed  (correct)
*   lon 7-8  DELEGATED BY AAAA TO BBBB     AC C -> CTA indexed via delegation marker
*   lon 8-9  GOLF TMA (stacked)   two bands, for the lowest-floor selection
*   lon 10-11 HOTEL UTMA SECTOR A AC C     -> TMA      Upper TMA (Polish spelling)
*   lon 11-12 INDIA / INDIA SECTOR B / INDIA CENTER SECTOR -- the GERMAN shape:
*            a CTR-class zone with an untyped shelf on top and an untyped
*            enroute block above. Only the stack walk can resolve it.
*            (lon 9-10 is left EMPTY on purpose -- it is the openair gap that
*             tests/test_openair_atcdat_fallback.cpp needs to reach atc.dat)
*
AC CTR
AN ALPHA CTR
AL GND
AH 2500 MSL
DP 40:00:00 N 000:00:00 E
DP 41:00:00 N 000:00:00 E
DP 41:00:00 N 001:00:00 E
DP 40:00:00 N 001:00:00 E
*

* lon 11-12: the GERMAN shape -- a CTR with an untyped shelf directly on top and
* an untyped enroute block far above it. Nothing here carries a type word, so
* the name-based lookup finds nothing and only the stack walk can answer.
